sanskrit_verse:
अपुत्रायोषितश्चैषां भर्तव्याः साधुवृत्तयः ।
निर्वास्या व्यभिचारिण्यः प्रतिकूलास्तथैव च ॥२.१४२
transliteration: aputrā yoṣitaś caiṣāṃ bhartavyāḥ sādhuvṛttayaḥ | nirvāsyā vyabhicāriṇyaḥ pratikūlās tathaiva ca || 2.142
sph_interpretive_translation: Women without sons must be maintained by righteous conduct; those who stray or oppose must be removed from association.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through alignment with Dharma, not biological lineage alone
Causation arises from integrity of action and relational harmony
Capacity-based responsibility requires protection for the vulnerable and conscious disengagement from harmful influence
Restoration logic mandates reintegration only where alignment with Satya is possible
Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for inclusion or exclusion in societal maintenance
executable_legal_axioms: IF a woman has no male heir AND maintains dharmic conduct THEN she shall receive sustenance from kin or community
IF a woman engages in vyabhicara (divergence from relational commitment) THEN severance of material support is mandated
IF a woman opposes dharma or disrupts familial/social order THEN exclusionary protocols apply without punitive intent
IF any individual's actions reduce collective consciousness THEN automatic withdrawal of facilitative structures occurs
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that dependency does not confer unqualified entitlement. Maintenance rights are conditional upon alignment with dharma. Straying from relational fidelity or opposing established dharmic order triggers lawful disassociation procedures, grounded not in punishment but in preservation of energetic coherence within society.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that misalignment creates natural separation; hence, removal serves correction, not condemnation. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how deviation leads to isolation as consequence, not imposed judgment. Proportional responsibility lies in recognizing one’s own role in disruption. The non-punitive reality rule confirms that all outcomes arise organically from consciousness distortion, requiring realignment rather than infliction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process to allow voluntary return to dharmic alignment before formal disengagement
Assign responsibility assumption protocol to family/community to ensure no abandonment occurs
Implement capacity restoration program for affected parties to reclaim self-supporting status
Activate integrity reintegration pathway if behavioral recalibration demonstrates readiness for renewed inclusion
final_declaration: This law originates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is hereby restored through alignment with Satya. There is no punishment—only consequence. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator.
